reading.body:
Meta does not publish power capacity for this campus, so its scale in the electricity market is unknown. The facility is one of 14 mapped data center locations in New Mexico and ranks first among them only by default, since no other facility in the state has published a megawatt figure. New Mexico has published zero megawatts of data center capacity across all mapped sites.

Meta invested $2.5 billion in this Valencia County campus starting from 2016 groundbreaking and reports 400-plus operational jobs once complete. At peak construction, 1,100 skilled workers were on site. The campus buildings achieve LEED Gold certification, which qualifies them for high-efficiency operational standards. Meta states that campus electricity use is matched with 100 percent renewable energy and that a Meta-supported project is adding 885 megawatts of new renewable energy and 100 megawatts of battery storage statewide.

The published specifications do not include total campus power draw, building count, square footage, or specific street address. Without a published power figure, this campus cannot be sized relative to other hyperscale AI facilities or assessed against grid constraints in its region. The investment and construction scale suggest a major facility, but the electricity demand that would determine its relevance to AI scaling remains undisclosed.
